title: Barakat Model
summary:
The Barakat Model is a scientifically validated session structure that brings aerobic, strength, flexibility, core, balance and pelvic floor work into the same sessions. It is built on six principles: maternal-fetal safety, constant professional supervision, regularity, a multicomponent approach, individualization and educational/motivational guidance.

The program runs from week 8-10 to week 38-39, three sessions per week of 50-60 min, with the share of each component shifting as pregnancy progresses. Each session has seven parts, from warm-up to a final discussion. The chapter also covers safe body positions, reported maternal and fetal benefits, and the model's limits: it complements, and does not replace, obstetric care.
points: The program runs from week 8-10 to week 38-39 with three sessions per week of 50-60 min.
Aerobic endurance share falls from 40% until week 20, to 30% until week 30, to 25% until week 38-39.
Pelvic floor training rises from 10% until week 20, to 15% until week 30, to 20% until week 38-39.
Strength is 30% until week 20 then 25%; coordination/balance and flexibility/relaxation are 10% then 15%; emotional management is treated every session.

A session has seven parts: warm-up (5-7 min), moderate aerobic (10-15 min), strength (10-12 min), coordination and balance (7-8 min), pelvic floor (8-10 min), cool-down (5-7 min) and a final discussion.
Aerobic work is at 55%-65% of heart rate reserve with perceived exertion 12-14 (somewhat hard); strength uses sets of 10-12 repetitions with light dumbbells or bands.
Supine positioning is limited to 2-3 min to avoid compression of the vena cava; side-lying is an excellent alternative.

Reported benefits include less excessive weight gain, lower risk of gestational diabetes, preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, less back pain and fatigue, and adequate birth weight with lower macrosomia risk.
Adherence should exceed 80% to obtain relevant clinical benefits.
takeaways: Aim for three supervised sessions a week of 50-60 min.
Keep aerobic effort at RPE 12-14 (somewhat hard).
Include pelvic floor work in every session and increase its share as pregnancy advances.
Use a stability ball when seated to reduce pelvic pressure.
Use a modified or side-lying position instead of lying on your back.
Work with a team such as an obstetrician, physiotherapist and exercise specialist.
cautions: Limit supine positioning to 2-3 min to avoid vena cava compression.
The model does not replace obstetric medical care.
Avoid impact activities in the warm-up.
